designSummary: Qualitative analysis; no statistical testing. Sample size set by information power and by the quotas needed to hear each group.
sampleSize: Information power guides the numbers: the aim is focused, the sample is specific, established concepts (trust, legitimacy) are used and the dialogue is in-depth, so about 24 parent interviews, 10 with dental teams and school nurses and 6 with councillors or campaigners should suffice, with four focus groups to test emerging themes. At least 12 of the 24 parents come from the two most deprived quintiles, and at least 4 interviews use interpreters. Recruitment continues past these numbers only if a quota group yields no new themes in its last three interviews.
primaryAnalysis: Reflexive thematic analysis of transcripts, coded by two analysts for a third of transcripts and by one thereafter, with themes developed across groups and compared by deprivation and role.
secondaryAnalysis: Framework matrix comparing themes by participant group; the anonymised consultation responses are coded with the same framework as context.
missingData: Not applicable in the statistical sense; groups that cannot be reached are reported as a limitation with the recruitment attempts made.
software: NVivo for coding; an audit trail of coding decisions.
overfittingGuards: Negative cases sought for each main theme
Themes checked with participants from each group before the report
summary: About 40 interviews and four focus groups by information power, with quotas for the most affected families.
